title: CS Quest 1.3 · If this, then that (Conditionals and events)
name: If this, then that (Conditionals and events)
summary: Students make Bolt decide for itself. In Robo Route the path ahead is hidden by fog, so a plain list of moves bumps the wall and an if block chooses instead; a when block lets something in the world start a piece of program. Levels with random layouts show why a program that checks beats a program that counts. Pairs share one device.
iCan: use an if block so Bolt decides for itself
use a when block so something happens on an event
say the difference between if and when
materials: If-Hat printable (a paper hat band, if cards, when cards)
doNow: If it rains at recess, then ___. Write two more if-then sentences about today.
plan: Explore: fog on level 1, then the event on level 2

warmup.why: two retrieval items from 1.2, one vocabulary item, one preview of today, one more from 1.2

do: Open Robo Route at Conditionals & events on the projector (Open game at this chapter). Level 1 has fog: Bolt cannot see whether the path ahead is open. Try a plain list first: forward, forward, forward. Run it. Bolt bumps the wall. Then delete it, add repeat 6, and inside it an if / else: if path ahead, forward; else, turn left. Run it and watch Bolt turn by itself at the wall.
Open level 2: every gem sits on a corner. Add a when block above the program: when gem, turn right. Then repeat 8 with forward and if gem, pick up. Run it: each pick-up turns Bolt.
say: A conditional lets the program choose. The if block asks a question about the world right now, and Bolt does one thing if the answer is yes and another if it is no.
A when block listens. It waits for something to happen, like picking up a gem, and runs its blocks right then. An if asks; a when listens.
ask: What is the difference between if and when?
explore.afterAsk: Write if and when on the board. Under if: asks a question now. Under when: waits for something to happen. Leave it up for Play.
explore.bigIdea: A conditional chooses; an event lets the world start a piece of program.

play.pairs: driver and navigator on one device; the Swap! banner shows every 3 levels; the navigator says the if sentence out loud (if ___ then Bolt ___) before the driver builds it
lookFors: kids who read if as a one-time check: step mode shows the check happening on every pass of the loop
the if placed outside the loop, so Bolt asks once and never again
on the random levels (3 to 7), pairs who keep the fixed list of moves and run it again hoping the board will match
play.misconception: An if inside a loop is not checked once: it is checked every time round, so Bolt can decide again at every square.
earlyFinishers: help a neighbor without touching their screen

unpluggedTwin.title: If-Hat
materials: one paper hat band per group
if cards (if I clap, hop; if I say blue, sit; if the light is off, freeze)
when cards (when the chime rings, stand; when someone sneezes, say bless you)
steps: The caller wears the hat and holds one if card. The caller does things: claps, says colors, waves. The group follows the card's rule only when its condition is true, and does nothing otherwise.
Swap the if card for an else card: if I clap, hop; else, clap back. Now the group always does something. Ask: which part ran, the if or the else?
Add a when card to the caller's hat. The when rule can fire at any moment, even in the middle of a round of if. Talk about why: an if asks when it is its turn; a when listens all the time.
Share: which rule was easiest to follow? When did someone act on a condition that was not true?

subPlan: Do Now on paper, 3 minutes: finish the sentence If it rains at recess, then ___, and write two more if-then sentences about today.

Play Robo Route, chapter Conditionals & events, in pairs for 20 minutes. Classes, then the lesson, then Play. If the game asks, the quest code is 3 1 0 0. Goal: 4 levels. No warm-up and no projector needed; playing signed out is fine.

Levels marked random run on three seeded layouts, so a fixed list of moves that works once fails on the next board. That failure is the lesson.
